title: P3: handover.py polish from approving review T-0180 (gitignore state, throttle under the flock, truncation test)
spec:
Low notes from the approving review of C-O7b (orchestrator/handover.py, `orchestrator handover`).
1. .gitignore gains .orchestrator/handover_state.json and .orchestrator/planner_session.json and .orchestrator/planner_usage.json and .orchestrator/planner_runs.json (operator state, never committed).
2. The handover throttle (last-written timestamp) is checked and updated inside the same flock as the plan.md write, so two daemons cannot both write within the interval.
3. The section-wide truncation branch (_join_truncated / MAX_ITEMS overflow) gets a test that renders more items than the cap and asserts the '… and N more' tail.
4. write() must not touch plan.md when the rendered Auto-handover section is byte-identical to the one already present (no dirtying the tracked file every 15 minutes with the same content).
Tests in tests/test_handover.py.
acceptance: tests/test_handover.py gains test_throttle_under_lock, test_truncation_tail, test_identical_section_does_not_rewrite and all pass

result.summary:
## Summary

Implemented all 4 low-severity C-O7b review notes, scoped to `orchestrator/handover.py`, `tests/test_handover.py`, `.gitignore`.

**Files changed:**
- `.gitignore`: added `.orchestrator/planner_runs.json` (the other three were already present).
- `orchestrator/handover.py`:
  - `write()` now compares the freshly rendered section against the section already on disk and returns early (no temp file / `os.replace`) when they're byte-identical.
  - Added `maybe_write(reason, now, interval)`: checks, writes, and saves the last-written timestamp all inside one `bus.locked()` acquisition, so a concurrent racing caller blocks on the flock instead of also passing the throttle check and double-writing.
- `tests/test_handover.py`: added `test_throttle_under_lock`, `test_truncation_tail`, `test_identical_section_does_not_rewrite`.

**Scope note:** `daemon.py` (which owns the tick loop's actual `maybe_handover` call) is outside this task's scope — the scope-guard hook blocked an edit there. Its existing check-then-write-then-save still isn't atomic under one lock. I added the properly-guarded `handover.maybe_write()` as the fix for the part reachable within scope; wiring `daemon.py`'s tick loop to call it instead of its own separate flock dance needs a follow-up task.

**Test output:** all 12 tests in `tests/test_handover.py` pass; `.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh` exits 0 (no failures to report).

Committed on `task/T-0204` as `02463d1`.
